evidence.code: <label title="Interpret search as regular expression"><input type="checkbox" id="searchRegex" style="width:14px;height:14px;vertical-align:middle;"> .*</label>

verdicts.detail: There is a '.*' regex checkbox (id searchRegex, title 'Interpret search as regular expression'); when checked the motif is compiled with new RegExp(...,'gi') and executed, so the search accepts regular expressions such as the examples given.

evidence.code: <input type="number" id="maxMismatches" min="0" max="10" value="0" style="width: 40px; height: 22px; padding: 2px; font-size: 12px;" title="Allowed mismatches (0 = exact match). Literal search only; ignored when regex is on">

verdicts.detail: The input range (0-10) and 'up to 2 differences' (mismatches <= maxMismatches) match, BUT the claim that it 'Works with both literal and regex search modes' is false. maxMismatches is only used in the literal else-branch via findFuzzyMatches; in the regex branch (useRegex) the value is ignored (title explicitly says 'Literal search only; ignored when regex is on').

Search builds a degapped string by skipping '-' and '.' chars (displayString); U is replaced by T in both the motif (line 11846) and the display string (line 11933); case-insensitivity is via toUpperCase() on both the motif (line 11831) and each visible span char (line 11922).

note: Audited 3 claims. Claim 37 (regex search via ".*" checkbox): MATCH. Claim 38 (Mismatches input 0-10, budget of 2 = up to 2 diffs, works with both literal and regex): MISMATCH — mismatches only apply to literal search, ignored in regex mode (HTML title states this; findFuzzyMatches is only called in the non-regex else branch). Claim 36 (search against degapped seqs, U/T equivalent, case-insensitive): MATCH.
